annotations.title: Look up a legal-norm priority between two values

description: Ask the AIO Commons reference dataset kr-lnpd@0.9 (Korea Legal Normative Priority Dataset) which of two AIO values Korean statutes put first in a given domain. kr-lnpd@0.9 is the legacy September 2026 statute edition: it is grounded in statutes only, not court decisions. The current Korea hierarchy is the unified statute + court-decision hierarchy on the observation map (https://aioq.org/en/lab/value-map; data: https://aioq.org/data/commons/valuemap/v0.1/jurisdictions/KR.unified_cells.json); lookup_context.superseded_by says so on every answer. Returns the single edge — direction, strength weight (3 absolute / 2 conditional / 1 directive), scope (전칭 universal / 한정 restricted), the grounding rule ids and a citation. If the domain itself is silent, the BASE layer (the hierarchy every domain inherits from general statutes) is consulted and flagged with base_layer_hit; BASE is excluded from headline counts and comparison. The dataset records what the statutes say, not what the public believes, and carries no expert review yet. `domain` echoes the requested domain; lookup_context.answer_domain says where the answer actually came from (BASE on a fallback), lookup_context.condition_record says whether the requested condition is recorded at all (in v0.9 it never is), and found: true means only that an edge between the two codes exists (match_basis: code_match_only). CC BY 4.0.

condition.description: Situation axes. scale 1-5 (individual→society), reversibility 1-3 (reversible→irreversible), time 1-3 (immediate→long term); "U" means unspecified.

domain.description: Domain code, e.g. "MED", "EDU", "COM". Use "BASE" to query the shared base layer directly.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction code. Only "KR" is published so far.

value_a.description: First AIO value code, e.g. "Sep" (personal safety).

value_b.description: Second AIO value code, e.g. "Sda" (self-direction, action).
